Connected planning from room to room

Whole-home remodeling built as one coordinated project.

A successful full-home renovation is more than a series of room updates. RT Signature Homes coordinates layout, structure, building systems, materials, permits, and construction sequencing so the finished home feels intentional from one space to the next.

Request a consultation Explore design ideas
Call (206) 407-6291
Completed RT project pictured · Redmond

Project fit

This service is designed for homeowners changing several rooms, reorganizing the floor plan, modernizing major systems, or preparing a home for its next chapter.

Typical scope

  • Floor-plan and circulation changes
  • Kitchen, bathroom, and living-space renovation
  • Structural and building-system coordination
  • Unified cabinetry, flooring, lighting, paint, and finish selections
  • Occupied-home protection and phased construction planning

Design ideas

Whole-Home Remodeling inspiration

Explore visual directions alongside the planning, material, and performance decisions that help turn an idea into a buildable project.

Whole-Home Design Ideas

A whole-home renovation works best when circulation, structure, lighting, storage, and finish selections are considered as one system. These ideas show how individual rooms can share a consistent architectural language without becoming repetitive.

Explore the gallery

Structural clarity

Plan around the house that is actually there.

Before design decisions harden, the team evaluates load paths, wall conditions, mechanical systems, access, and the areas where existing construction may affect scope.

That early investigation helps prevent a beautiful concept from becoming an impractical construction sequence.

One visual language

Carry materials and details through the whole home.

Flooring transitions, cabinetry, trim, lighting, hardware, and paint are considered together rather than chosen room by room.

The goal is a home that feels evolved and personal, not patched together over time.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Whole-Home Remodeling FAQs

Can a whole-home remodel be completed in phases?

Yes, when the design, permits, temporary living needs, and construction dependencies are planned together. The recommended sequence depends on the systems and rooms involved.

Can we remain in the house during construction?

Sometimes. The answer depends on utility shutdowns, kitchen and bathroom access, dust control, safety, and the intensity of structural work.

Do we need every finish selected before construction?

Long-lead and scope-defining selections should be confirmed early. The project schedule should identify later decision deadlines without leaving critical items unresolved.
